subject: Clarification and Attestation: Vulnerability Scan Program & CVE Remediation Commitments
messages:
From: DevSec Team <devsec@keystonebank.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: security-audit@keystonebank.com
Date: 2026-10-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: VM program details and remediation evidence for SIG/SOC2 review

Hi Laura,

We're preparing the SIG intake for Keystone Bank's upcoming vendor review (week of Nov 15) and need a compact evidence packet covering Redwood's vulnerability management program. Specifically we need: 
- Recent (last 90 days) authenticated scan cadence and summary for any production-facing services used by Keystone.
- SLA / remediation timelines for high/critical CVEs, including examples of closure timelines for two representative CVEs.
- A short attestation that exceptions are tracked and reviewed, with links to any open exception register or compensating control details.

Can you provide the packet and a signed attestation (PDF) by EOD Nov 2? If you have a standard SOC2/SIG supplement that covers scan frequency and CVE handling, that would be great.

Thanks,
Marcus Reed
Senior DevSec Engineer
Keystone Bank

(Attachment: none)

Kimberly / SecOps: can you assemble a compact packet (PDF + manifest) that includes:

- Patch manifest + ticket references for two CVEs we closed in the last 60 days.
- Exception register excerpt (if any) and compensating controls.

Ben / Monica: flag if Keystone needs a point on commercial terms or executive attestation. Marcus asked for signed attestation by COB Nov 2 — I can sign once SecOps confirms.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: DevSec Team <devsec@keystonebank.com>
Date: 2026-10-31T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: VM program details and remediation evidence for SIG/SOC2 review

Laura / team / Marcus — attaching the requested artifacts. Summary below; full packet is Q3-2026-vm-scan-summary.pdf and patch_manifest_20261029.csv attached.

Key points (short):
- Tooling & cadence: Authenticated scans run against prod-like clusters weekly (Nessus authenticated, internal agent scans daily for container images). Broad surface scans are scheduled weekly; targeted authenticated scans run every 7 days for externally facing services and every 30 days for internal infra.
- SLA definitions: Critical (0–7 days from discovery), High (0–30 days), Medium (0–90 days), Low (best-effort, tracked). Emergency hotfix channel exists for active exploitation.
- Recent closures (examples):
  * CVE-2026-2248 (openssl component) — discovered 2026-09-18, ticket RWD-4591, patch deployed and verified 2026-09-23 (5 days) — evidence in patch_manifest_20261029.csv and ticket link in PDF.
  * CVE-2026-4010 (third-party lib) — discovered 2026-10-03, rollback mitigated and patch by 2026-10-12 (9 days) with compensating control active 2026-10-04 — traces and verification steps in PDF.
- Exceptions: We maintain an exception register; current open exceptions relevant to Keystone are operationally isolated and the compensating control is network-level filtering + additional host-based detection (details in PDF excerpt).

Attachments: Q3-2026-vm-scan-summary.pdf (6 pages), patch_manifest_20261029.csv (3 columns: cve_id, ticket_id, closure_date), remediation-attestation-laura-signed.pdf (signed attestation draft).

Marcus — if you want a short narrative attestation for SIG that references our SOC2 control mapping, we can add a single-paragraph addendum. Laura, once you sign the attached PDF I’ll route final package to Marcus and upload to the Drive link.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security Engineer, SecOps
Redwood Inference

(Attachments: Q3-2026-vm-scan-summary.pdf (summary), patch_manifest_20261029.csv (manifest), remediation-attestation-laura-signed.pdf (draft signature))

Thanks Kim — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions before we close the packet: 
1) For the ‘Critical = 0–7 days’ SLA, how do you measure the start time? Is it vulnerability discovery by internal scanner, vendor disclosure, or when a ticket is created? Please state the formal measurement point.
2) For exceptions, can you confirm whether compensating controls are validated quarterly or on a per-release basis?

Also — could you include the ticket IDs for the two CVEs in the attestation text (so the auditor can cross-check)? We saw RWD-4591 in the manifest but would like the ticket links if possible.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Marcus

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: DevSec Team <devsec@keystonebank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T14:55:00-07:00
Subject: Final: VM attestation and clarifications for Keystone Bank SIG packet

Marcus — thanks for the questions. Final clarifications and attestation below; attached is a signed PDF (remediation-attestation-laura-signed.pdf) and I uploaded the packet to Drive (link below).

Answers:
- SLA measurement point: SLA starts when the vulnerability is recorded in our ticketing system (ticket creation time). We ingest findings from scanners, bug bounties, vendor advisories into an automated triage pipeline; the clock for SLA begins when a remediation ticket is created and prioritized in the RWD tracker.
- Exception validation cadence: Compensating controls are reviewed quarterly (security-design review) and validated on any production-facing release that touches the exception scope. The exception register excerpt in the PDF lists last validation dates.
- Ticket links for the two example CVEs: RWD-4591 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RWD-4591), RWD-4723 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RWD-4723). Both links are in the patch manifest and the PDF evidence.

Attestation (signed):
"Redwood Inference hereby attests that, as of Nov 2, 2026, the attached vulnerability management artifacts accurately reflect our operating VM program for production-facing services used by Keystone Bank. Our SLA definitions and remediation timelines are applied consistently; exceptions are tracked and reviewed as described. We commit to providing follow-up evidence for any auditor requests within reasonable operational bounds"

If Keystone needs the attestation on company letterhead routed through DocuSign, I included a DocuSign route in related links. Otherwise the attached signed PDF should satisfy the SIG packet.

Ben / Monica: please confirm if you want Sales to forward the packet via HubSpot or share Drive link directly with their audit team.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

(Attachments: remediation-attestation-laura-signed.pdf)
